prompt: Combine two Optionals into one: write a generic combine that produces a value only when both are present, then build two small helpers on top of it.
explanation: Optional has no built-in zip, so combining two of them means nesting: flatMap on the first hands you its value only if it is present, and map on the second wraps the merged result -- flatMap on the outside is what keeps the type Optional<R> rather than Optional<Optional<R>>. Both lambdas are only evaluated on the present path, so a merger that would fail on missing data is simply never called. Writing it once as a generic helper means label and sum are single lines that share the whole empty-handling story.
hints: The outer call must be flatMap and the inner one map; swapping them gives a nested Optional that will not compile.
merger.apply(a, b) is how you invoke a BiFunction inside the inner lambda.
label and sum should not repeat any Optional logic -- each is a single return combine(...) with a two-argument lambda.
